environment: Disposable Linux ARM64 VM, 1 CPU and 2 GiB RAM; isolated host-side Git transport
method: A synthetic local Git repository, deterministic public test seed, nonsecret profile inputs and synthetic files were used. The complete checkpoint CLI captured a signed envelope including a dirty tracked file and an untracked executable; verify and restore succeeded. Incorrect epoch and author were refused. CLI closure selected only verified CID blocks. A human-equivalent host-side Git invocation stored those synthetic blocks and manifest in a private GitHub test ref without force; a separate bare repository fetched the ref, matched its tree and ran git fsck. The independently fetched blocks were copied back into the VM; the same native CLI verified the signed contract and restored the dirty tracked file and executable with mode 0755.
limits: The signing seed and all data are synthetic and nonsecret. GitHub transfer was a one-off operator-side Git procedure, not a native autonomous archive component or an active bot turn. GitHub privacy was verified immediately before the push. The compiler is a byte-patched test copy, not a self-built or released compiler. No Darwin runtime, multi-host fencing, production credential boundary, or fleet resource governor was qualified.
